title: Taylor Convergence for Bounded-Derivative Smooth Functions

problemStatement.formal: If f : ℝ → ℝ is C^∞ and ∃ C ≥ 0, ∀ n x, ‖iteratedDeriv n f x‖ ≤ C, then Tendsto (taylorPartialSum f · x) atTop (𝓝 (f x))
problemStatement.plain: Prove that for any smooth real function whose iterated derivatives are uniformly bounded, the Taylor partial sums at 0 converge pointwise to the function.
whyMatters: Generalizes specific sin/cos convergence to an abstract framework
Shows the convergence mechanism depends only on derivative bounds, not algebraic structure

knownResults.goal: General Taylor convergence for bounded-derivative functions

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: TaylorSinCosConvergenceOQ04.lean now has 18 public theorems, 1 def, 0 local axioms, and 0 sorries. The general_taylor_remainder_bound proof uses reflection via iteratedDeriv_comp_neg, while linear_combo_bound is proved with smul linearity lemmas; the imported parent proof still carries its own two remainder-bound axioms.
insights: Taylor convergence depends only on two properties: smoothness and uniform derivative bound. Period-4, parity, etc. are irrelevant to the convergence mechanism.
The x < 0 case is handled by reflecting g(t)=f(-t) and applying iteratedDeriv_comp_neg.
By Bernstein's theorem, functions with uniformly bounded derivatives are exactly bounded entire functions of exponential type ≤ 1 (trigonometric polynomials with freq ≤ 1).
Sin/cos achieve the minimum bound C = 1 among non-constant functions in this class.
Proved general_taylor_remainder_bound by reflection: g(t)=f(-t), using iteratedDeriv_comp_neg (no hypotheses needed in Mathlib). This eliminates the 1 axiom.
